author: LeadershipNGA
title: BSE Eyes African Expansion Through Mauritius‑Based Afrinex, CEOs Highlight Investor Protections and Global Connectivity
text:
The Bombay Stock Exchange announced its strategy to deepen ties with African markets through Afrinex, a Mauritius‑based multi‑currency exchange. Managing Director Sundararaman Ramamurthy outlined the platform's role, India's robust derivatives market, investor protection mechanisms and technology backbone, while also noting existing conduits such as ETFs, mutual funds and GIFT City that link Indian and international investors. The news reflects India's ambition to become a gateway for African nations into global financial markets.
During a high‑profile open house for a delegation of international journalists, Sundararaman Ramamurthy, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Bombay Stock Exchange ( BSE), articulated a bold new vision for deepening economic ties between India and Africa.
He revealed that the BSE is in the process of establishing a partnership with Afrinex, a Mauritius‑based multi‑currency and multi‑asset exchange that has received backing from the Government of Mauritius and will be powered by the BSE's technology infrastructure. Ramamurthy described Afrinex as a "gateway" that will enable African countries-including Nigeria-to access Indian capital markets and, by extension, global markets.
He emphasized that the platform aims to bridge currency, regulatory, and market access gaps, providing a single point through which the continent can engage with the world's most dynamic financial ecosystem. In addition, the BSE's CEO highlighted India's maturity in the derivatives space, noting that trading volumes and participation have grown steadily since the 1970s when derivatives were first introduced on a global level.
While he did not disclose specific figures, he indicated that India now captures a substantial share of global stock‑index options activity. This development further underscores the country's role as an attractive destination for sophisticated investors seeking exposure to a broad range of asset classes. Investor protection and market integrity were key themes in Ramamurthy's remarks.
He pointed out that India's use of dematerialised (Demat) accounts-electronic holding systems where securities are credited directly to investors-combined with stringent settlement guarantees, effectively reduces transaction risk. The BSE's settlement cycle operates on a T+1 basis, meaning trades are settled one business day after execution, and the system logs every transaction in a transparent audit trail.
Ramamurthy said that this infrastructure, powered by advanced technology, supports transparency and orderly market behaviour, which is essential for attracting both domestic and foreign participants. He also noted a mix of products, large number of market members, and substantial foreign participation that all benefit from the BSE's robust technology backbone. Beyond Afrinex, Ramamurthy pointed to several other mechanisms that already connect Indian and international investors.
These include exchange‑traded funds and mutual funds with overseas exposure, and the Liberalised Remittance Scheme which permits eligible Indian residents to invest abroad within specified limits. The BSE also has ongoing collaboration with Gujarat International Finance Tec‑City (GIFT City), a purpose‑built financial hub designed to provide a platform for international investors to access Indian and global financial products. Together, these channels build a comprehensive and layered environment where cross‑border capital flows can occur smoothly.
The delegation's visit concluded with a market‑closing bell ceremony in which media representatives joined the BSE staff and honored the end of the trading day. This public‑relations event demonstrated the BSE's openness and commitment to engaging with the global press and investors. The conversation around BSE's expansion into Africa, paired with India's strong institutional framework, signals a new chapter in the country's push to become the ultimate gateway for emerging markets in the 21st century.
Over the coming months, the BSE and Afrinex will work on operationalizing the platform, designing regulatory compliance frameworks, and engaging with African financial authorities to ensure a seamless entry into the Indian market. If successful, Africans will enjoy access to a diverse suite of Indian equities, bonds, and derivative instruments-all while benefiting from India's world‑class investor protection and settlement mechanisms
